semantics: os.access(Path(file), os.X_OK) -> True iff path exists AND caller has execute permission
rationale: The predicate is a live filesystem probe (os.access X_OK). Its truth value is determined entirely by external state (path existence + execute permission bits), not by any symbolic boolean/integer/comparison structure over the public CLI input `file`. z3 cannot constrain the filesystem, so solver_status=unknown for the concrete predicate. A boolean ABSTRACTION (access == exists AND executable) is trivially SAT for both branches (solver_models), and a pure helper modeling that abstraction was checked with CrossHair (no counterexample, exit 0).
encoder_boundary: Op-surface from Configuration.py ExpressionEvaluator (boolean/compare/arith/bit/unary/conditional) does not apply: the predicate is a single opaque call (os.access) over a filesystem path string. No arithmetic/comparison sub-structure to encode; the only tractable model is the boolean abstraction below.

true_examples.note: Confirmed by running _exeExists(Path('/usr/bin/g++')) in tl-char (real filesystem). Drives true_branch: return file.

false_examples.note: Path does not exist. Drives false_branch: raise FileNotFoundError.
Exists but no execute bit (chmod 0o644). Also drives false_branch: raise FileNotFoundError.

pure_helper:
def exe_exists_model(exists: bool, executable: bool) -> bool:
    """Pure model of _exeExists(Path(file)) == os.access(file, os.X_OK).

    post: __return__ == (exists and executable)
    post: __return__ <= exists
    """
    return exists and executable

crosshair.caveat: Absence of a counterexample is NOT a proof; CrossHair explores bounded paths/time.
